rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Now the king, the most important piece: losing the king means losing the game. He is on d4.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: He moves in any direction, like the queen, but only one square at a time.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: From d4 there are eight possible squares: all the neighbouring ones.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Take the king to e5, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The king takes one step diagonally, to e5.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: The king went to another neighbouring square. Let's go back: the target is e5, diagonally up.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Take the king to e5, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: Then one more step: upwards this time.
rot.ideia.ex1.l3: Each move, one square only. To go far, the king needs many moves.
rot.ideia.ex1.l4: Remember the idea: the king moves one square at a time, in any direction.
rot.ideia.ex1.l5: Now the rule that only the king has.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: Now there are black pieces, the opponent's: the king on a8 and a rook on f8. They stay still.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: It reaches the whole f-file, down to f1.
rot.ideia.ex2.e3: The king may never go to a square an enemy piece reaches: the whole f-file is forbidden.
rot.ideia.ex2.e4: Your goal is to take the king to e3, in two moves.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: What is the king's first move towards e3? Suggest one, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! From e2 the king already touches e3.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: One step up, to e2; the f-file stays aside.
rot.ideia.ex2.alt.e1d2.1: That works too! From d2 the king also touches e3.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.e1d1.1: From d1 the king is still two steps from e3.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.e1d1.2: That would make three moves. Let's go back and get closer.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: What is the king's first move towards e3? Suggest one, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: One more step and the king reaches e3.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: The king stayed away from the f-file, which the rook watches.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Via d2 would also work, in two moves.
rot.ideia.ex2.l4: Remember the idea: the king only steps on squares the opponent does not reach.
rot.ideia.ex2.l5: You have now seen the king's two rules. Now I will show them in other positions.
rot.demos.canto.e1: Look at the king in the corner, on a1.
rot.demos.canto.e2: Here he has only three squares: a2, b2 and b1.
rot.demos.canto.l1: One step towards the centre, and he has eight squares again.
rot.demos.canto.l2: In the corner the king is cramped; in the centre, free.
rot.demos.marcha.e1: The king on e1 wants to reach e8, on the other side.
rot.demos.marcha.l3: ...and so, step by step through e4, e5, e6 and e7, only on the seventh move does he reach e8.
rot.demos.marcha.l4: The queen would do it in a single move. The king is slow: plan his route ahead.
rot.demos.doisReis.e1: Now both kings, the white one on e4 and the black one on e6.
rot.demos.doisReis.e2: The squares d5, e5 and f5 touch both kings.
rot.demos.doisReis.e3: The black king reaches those squares, so the white king may not step on them.
rot.demos.doisReis.l1: He moves sideways, away from the black king.
rot.demos.doisReis.l2: The two kings never touch, neither side by side nor diagonally: there is always a square between them.
rot.demos.doisReis.l3: Now it's your turn: in the next positions, take the king to the stars.
rot.pratica.estrelas1.enunciado: Take the king to the three stars, stopping on each one, in any order you like.
rot.pratica.estrelas1.fim: Perfect. Step by step, counting the moves, the king gets where he wants.
rot.pratica.estrelas2.enunciado: The black king is on e4: the squares around him are forbidden. Take your king to the stars.
rot.pratica.estrelas2.fim: Well done. You now know how to move the king: one square at a time and never onto a square the opponent reaches.
